decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core cheese range that remained prominently presented after launch, Product C likely met or exceeded the firm's aspiration level and fits existing organic dairy resources well, so management would keep it.

Because Product D built on the established cheese offer and advanced from a mention to its own page, its observed acceptance appears satisfactory relative to aspiration levels, making retention the likely boundedly rational choice.

Product E was explicitly highlighted at launch and then given its own page, which suggests performance good enough to justify continued support within the firm's focused, sustainability-based portfolio.

Product F disappeared from the website by 2019, indicating results below aspiration or insufficient promise, so a Behavioral Theory of the Firm response would be to reallocate its resources to stronger core products or new search.
